title: Great Bottle But Very Overpriced
text:
Great Bottle But Very Overpriced. I prefer glass bottles to plastic and metal, so the Soma water bottle is a good choice for me. It’s made well and it looks great. The only reservation I have about it – the price.

The bottle is heavy glass borosilicate. This particular type of glass is somewhat more resistant to shattering, though its strength is in being fairly impervious to rapid temperature changes. This bottle is not designed to be used for hot beverages so I suspect it could have been made with a lower grade of glass and still be shatter-resistant. It’s not unwelcome, either way. Because it is glass and not plastic, it doesn’t stain which is great when you fill it with something colorful and fair to wash it afterward – it still comes clean.

The bottle has a rubbery sleeve that serves two purposes. First, it is an insulator and it will keep you from freezing your hands when drinking something very cold. Second, if your hands are wet it is still sufficient to help you maintain a good, solid grip on the bottle.

The cap is the weak point though it is relative. It is plastic on the inside, with a heavy bamboo outer shell to protect it. It will likely survive it you drop it, though it seems like this is the one part that is most likely to fail. So far, I have used the bottle and kept the cap on a nearby shelf, so I don’t have an opportunity to drop it but this is more so I won’t actually misplace it.

My one concern with this bottle is the actual cost. As I write this, the bottle is selling for $25-$30 based on color and that’s just absurd. I can see asking between $15-$20 at most. At $30 though (I have the white one), I will not replace it when and if I somehow manage to break it.

Other than being priced unreasonably high, this is a nice water bottle. It has some heft to it, it can survive short drops and jostles, it has a non-slip sleeve and it looks great. Before buying, though, wait for the price to come down or catch it on sale.
